title: Matched buoy changes show no clear extra loss of daily OISST cooling response in 2022-2025
abstract: We tested whether the recent fall in OISST response to buoy changes was greater for cooling than for warming. We compared 2016-2019 with 2022-2025 in a verified daily archive. A continuous piecewise linear fit used common calendar-month and change-magnitude bins in both directions and eras. At 67 stations, the one-day cooling slope fell by 0.169 and the warming slope by 0.108. The extra cooling loss was 0.061, with a 95% spatial-group interval of -0.002 to 0.143. Seven-day changes at 29 stations gave -0.008 (-0.079 to 0.052). Network and model checks did not give a common direction result. A separate held-out-year test found no mean error reduction from separate direction slopes. In 19 eligible recent-era daily stations, the direction model raised error by 0.18%. The main result is unresolved direction dependence, not equal response. The overall response loss remains in the tested linear model. The study uses the same archive as prior response studies. Buoy assimilation, point-to-grid mismatch, short eras, conditional spatial intervals and limited common support prevent a global or causal interpretation. We provide original code, aggregate results, input hashes, a figure, an independent algebra audit and exact retrieval instructions. External daily records and record-level derivatives remain outside the publication.

display.caption: OISST response to cooling and warming buoy changes in 2016-2019 and 2022-2025. Support is matched by month and magnitude bin. Bars show conditional 95% spatial-group intervals. Samples have 67 stations at one day and 29 at seven days.
